verdict: Chemists found little evidence the compounds are novel and useful.
detail: A UC Santa Barbara review found scant evidence of compounds that are new, credible and useful. DeepMind stands by the paper.

claim: FunSearch discovered a new solution to an open math problem
verdict: Published in Nature: an LLM-guided search beat human records on the cap set problem.
detail: FunSearch paired an LLM with an automated evaluator to evolve Python programs, finding larger cap sets in 8 dimensions than previously known.

claim: ESM3 generated a new fluorescent protein equal to 500M years of evolution
verdict: Peer-reviewed in Science: esmGFP glows in the lab with only 58% sequence identity.
detail: The 98B-parameter protein language model designed a functional green fluorescent protein far from any natural sequence, verified experimentally.

claim: AI co-scientist matched 10 years of lab work in 2 days
verdict: Its top hypothesis matched the lab's finding, later published in Cell.
detail: The Imperial College team had unpublished data; Google confirmed no leak. Other models failed the same test.

claim: Vibe-coded a multiplayer 3D flight sim in 3 hours that hit $87k/mo
verdict: The live browser game went viral on X; revenue figures are self-reported.
detail: Built with Cursor and Three.js, fly.pieter.com drew hundreds of thousands of players and sold in-game blimp ads. Peak MRR comes from creator posts with no independent audit.

claim: AlphaEvolve broke a 56-year-old matrix multiplication record
verdict: It found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices, beating Strassen's 49.
detail: The Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent beat Volker Strassen's 1969 bound and also discovered scheduling and kernel improvements used inside Google.

claim: An AI won gold at the Math Olympiad
verdict: DeepMind's proofs were graded by official IMO coordinators.
detail: Gemini Deep Think scored 35 of 42 in contest time. OpenAI's same score was graded by former medalists, not the IMO.

claim: Evo AI generated the first functional whole-genome viruses
verdict: 16 AI-designed bacteriophage genomes replicated and lysed E. coli in the lab.
detail: Using Evo genome language models, researchers chemically synthesized ~300 candidates and recovered 16 viable phages, some outperforming natural phiX174.

claim: Agents built a web browser from scratch in a week
verdict: It renders pages, but builds failed and code reuse was questioned.
detail: Over 1M lines were written. Reviewers found failing builds; critics said it leaned on Servo, which Cursor denies.

claim: 16 Claude agents built a Rust C compiler that compiles Linux
verdict: Open-sourced in Rust; compiles bootable Linux 6.9, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Doom.
detail: Parallel Claude Opus 4.6 agents wrote 100k+ lines over two weeks. Caveats: it uses GCC for 16-bit x86 real mode and produces slower binaries than GCC or Clang.

claim: One engineer rebuilt Next.js on Vite with AI in a week
verdict: Open-sourced as vinext; built for ~$1,100 in tokens and passes Next.js E2E tests.
detail: Across 800+ AI coding sessions, vinext reimplemented the Next.js API surface on Vite for Cloudflare Workers, verified with thousands of Vitest and 380+ Playwright tests.

claim: Autoresearch lets an AI agent run ML experiments overnight
verdict: The viral open-source loop works on toy runs; real frontier gains aren't proven yet.
detail: The minimalist GitHub repo lets coding agents edit train.py in 5-minute GPU loops and keep wins via git, sparking thousands of forks on X, though independent research breakthroughs remain early.

claim: An amateur solved Erdős #1196 with one prompt
verdict: Mathematicians checked it and it was verified in Lean.
detail: The 60-year-old problem is marked solved. Experts said the approach surprised them.

claim: Bun was rewritten from Zig to Rust in 11 days
verdict: It shipped as Bun 1.4 and passed the full test suite.
detail: 64 Claude agents ported ~535,000 lines. Zig's creator called it unreviewed.
